title: Runtime version safety protocols and client adapter compatibility contract
creator: Priya Khosla
description: Purpose: Define an actionable, runtime-focused semantic-versioning and rollout contract that protects customers and internal services when we ship changes to the serving runtime. This ticket collects the protocol-level rules (headers, forward/back-compat guarantees), LTS cadence and windows, explicit rollback triggers, and a small set of CLI and CI tools that make upgrades measurable and reversible. Goal is to reduce customer incidents from runtime upgrades and make safe rollouts the default for all changes that touch the public binary protocol, KV cache formats, or RPC behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable doc outlining: compatibility guarantees by version class (patch/minor/major) and examples specific to serving runtime (kernel selection, KV cache format, model signature changes).
A machine-readable compatibility header and protocol that the runtime emits (X-Runtime-Version and X-Compat-Mode) and a spec for client adapters to detect and fail fast with guidance.
A minimal 'amcli compat-check' command that warns about client-server version skew and returns non-zero for dangerous combinations.
Canary rollout recipe described (percentiles, duration, health signals, auto-rollback thresholds) and added to the release checklist.
E2E compatibility test added to CI that runs against latest LTS image and the candidate nightly for at least 3 key APIs.
Migration assistant prototype that produces a 'migration report' for customers showing required steps and estimated surface area for changes classified as breaking.
rollout_gates: Gate 1 (Pre-release): CI compat-suite must pass against LTS images for 24 hours.
Gate 2 (Canary): Deploy candidate to 3% of traffic in US region for min 6 hours with 99th percentile latency within 1.5x baseline and error budget consumption <10%.
Gate 3 (Staged ramp): Increase to 20% for 24 hours if no alerts; run full compatibility suite against live telemetry snapshots.
Gate 4 (Wide): 100% rollout with extended monitoring and forced client adapter compatibility warnings posted to Console if any non-fatal incompat signals appear.

Auto-rollback: trigger if any of the following occur: sustained p50 latency >2x baseline for 10 minutes, new 5xx rate >0.5% absolute increase, or meaningful increase in client-side Compat-Failure metric.
deprecation_policy: Deprecation header: runtime will emit 'X-Runtime-Deprecation: <feature>:<date>' and Console will show deprecation banners 90 days prior to removal.
Soft deprecation window: 90 days for non-critical features; recommended migration helpers provided in SDKs.
Extended deprecation window: 180 days for commonly used public APIs (generation/chat/embeddings endpoints).
Critical-security removals: may be accelerated with a minimum 30-day notice plus emergency migration paths and partner outreach.
breaking_change_classification: Category A (Allowed non-breaking): kernel micro-optimizations, internal scheduling reseeds that do not change binary protocol or persisted formats.

Category B (Potentially breaking): changes to request/response envelope fields, optional arguments moved to required, or changes to default quantization profiles. Requires client adapter patch and compat tests.
Category C (Breaking): wire protocol changes, KV cache on-disk format changes, auth handshake changes, or removal of response fields. Requires major version and migration plan.
upgrade_tooling: amcli compat-check --server-version <v> --client-version <v>: exit non-zero for Category B/C mismatches and print recommended shim or SDK patch.
amcli dry-run-upgrade --image <candidate>: runs compat-suite in an isolated environment against a snapshot of production traces.
compat-harness CI job: runs fuzzed RPCs and serialized KV cache round-trips between candidate and LTS images.
migration-assistant (prototype): produces a human-readable report with file-level diffs, impacted routes, and estimated developer effort.
telemetry_signals: compat.failure.count (counter) - incremented when client encounters incompatibility header
migration_paths: Minor upgrade (patch/minor with no protocol changes): automatic; advise clients to update SDK within 1 release cycle.
In-place migration (cache or default behavior change): runtime ships a compatibility shim for 2 release cycles; SDK emits warnings and optional flag to opt-in to new behavior.
Major migration (protocol or on-disk format): publish migration guide, provide conversion tool, mark old LTS as security-fix-only for 1 year.
compatibility_tests: Round-trip KV cache validation with seed corpus (permits small non-determinism margin).
RPC contract tests that validate envelopes and optional/required fields across versions.
Synthetic production replay against candidate runtime for top 50 routes by QPS.
SDK adapter matrix: for each supported SDK version, run the compat-suite against candidate and supported LTS versions.
risks_mitigation: Risk: silent client failures when defaults change. Mitigation: require explicit opt-in for default behavior flips and emit deprecation headers well in advance.
Risk: long-lived forks of client adapters missing security fixes. Mitigation: SDKs will show EOL warnings for adapters older than 12 months in Console.
Risk: inadequate canary signal coverage. Mitigation: synthetic replay and traffic shadowing to supplement production canaries.
